newsitem.title: BELGIUM: DG X safe from major shake-up -- for now.
newsitem.headline: DG X safe from major shake-up -- for now.

text.p: The European Commission's Directorate General X -- responsible for information, communication, culture and the audiovisual media -- has avoided a major reorganisation after months of speculation.

Culture Commissioner Marcelino Oreja told Reuters in a telephone interview DG X would not give up any of its functions, but that the EU executive had accepted his plan to restructure its operations to create an information centre.

"There are no changes in the competence of DG X. There are no changes unless there's the agreement of the commissioners," Oreja said, stressing he would never have given his approval for such a change.

After months of speculation over who would replace Lusembourg's Colette Flesch as director general, Commission sources say that the current Greek director general for consumer policy, Spyros Pappas, is hot favourite to secure the post.
That appointment would put an end to rumours that the Commission's chief spokesman, Nikolaus van der Pas, would move to head DG X. Van der Pas told Reuters he was not a candidate for the post.

One option for a more radical shake-up which was rejected would have moved the spokesman's service from under the wing of Commission President Jacques Santer to DG X, while farming out audiovisual policy to three other directorates general.
Under another option backed by French commissioners, an audiovisual task force, comprised of members of different DGs, would have been set up.
In the end Oreja gained backing to reorganise DG X to create a public information centre that would cooperate with national organisations.
"We want to create a centre, an agency of information in close cooperation with the other bureaus," he said.
He declined to be drawn on the name of the successor to Flesch, who will move to head the translation service in Luxembourg at the beginning of next year.
Even though DG X has been spared a major reorganisation at this point, EU officials expect that a change could take place at the beginning of the new Commission.
Among the possibilities are that a special directorate general responsible for new media services would bet set up, covering things like audivisual policy and the Internet.
